entrenched.description: Obedience is the core of any military, and failure to follow the Commandant's orders always meant a bullet to the back of the skull. The Entrenced proves Craie's military discipline must be better than he previously thought, as she will strive to do literally anything he asks.

monitor.description: The Commandant spent his career fighting Ostvengr's army, and rates its officers highly. He holds nothing personal against this one. He knows the country is gone, and wants to know what a staff officer of theirs is doing this far south, and if he'll obey orders.

rampart.description: The Commandant's forces have fought the Rampart many times on the battlefield: the sight of it was a cue to retreat, and let his colleagues advance elsewhere. He will enjoy fighting alongside this age-old enemy.

slayer.description: The Commandant's forces fought Ostvengr's well-trained Slayer corps for generations on the battlefield. Taking one down was a monumental achievement. This one seems far worse than the rest, and the Commandant is glad to stand alongside one for once.

heiress.description: The crusader maintains a professional relationship with the heiress, focusing on fulfilling his role as her protector with a devout sense of duty.

highwayman.description: The Crusader recognizes something familiar in the Highwayman's bearing - another man haunted by his past. He wonders if they might find common ground, though trust must be earned.

kheir.description: The Crusader has pledged to protect the Heir despite obvious doubts about his fitness for the trials ahead. He sees a frightened scholar where leadership is needed, but duty demands he try.

seraph.description: The Crusader served under the Seraph after her miraculous transformation, awed by her divine presence and inspired by her holy purpose. Her burned visage and manifest powers were proof of the Light's grace, making his role in her crusade feel truly righteous.

heiress.description: To the Duchess, the young Heiress was an unremarkable presence, noteworthy only because of her name and connection to the Ancestor. The Duchess has forgotten her.

hqclaimants.description: The Duchess saw the Claimants as scheming has-beens beneath her station, their fading influence barely worth acknowledging amid her greater rivalry with the Countess.

kheir.description: In her brief early encounters with the Heir, the Duchess found his adoration amusing but ultimately inconsequential. She does not remember him.

thorn.description: The Duchess remembers the celebrated Rose—the one blade at court worth measuring against her own. A grand tournament was to settle it at last, in a final all of society anticipated; instead the Rose fell to an unremarkable blade in an earlier bout, blinded, and the Duchess claimed her championship by walkover. Her pride has never forgiven the debt that can no longer be collected.

aesthete.description: The Arbiter walked away from the Coven and its methods, and has spent every day since being sure enough of that. Then a lord arrives keeping bird-folk as household ornaments, groomed and owned. The man is not cruel and does not think himself an enemy, which is worse. The Arbiter will be civil, because saying anything true would mean explaining who he is.

man_at_arms.description: When the Arbiter's squad was hunted down for deserting, a stranger arrived in the middle of it and fought the Coven off long enough for two of them to get clear. The Arbiter never learned why a human soldier would do that for a bird, and never got the chance to ask. He owes this man his life and intends to say so at the first opportunity.

commandant.description: The Entrenched has been waiting for someone with rank to arrive. Craie and Chernozem fought the same enemy, which as far as she is concerned makes him her commanding officer. She will salute, report, and obey without question or hesitation.

dredge.description: Ostvengr's dredge corps excavated the tec and built the ingenious machines that served as the foundation of the empire's military dominance. After its fall, Craie and the other neighbours shut the border and refused refugees. The Entrenched sees no reason to be the exception. The war ends when they are all gone.

monitor.description: Ostvengr took the Entrenched's parents and her home, and its fall was supposed to end the war. But here, the last officer of that empire is cheerfully recruiting for its next army. As far as the Entrenched is concerned their nations are still at war, and enemy officers are to be killed on sight.

rampart.description: Every army that faced Ostvengr had a story about the black shell: the Rampart that could not be stopped or killed, that came through a line and left it gone. Born to officers, she was practically raised on those horror stories. She will be frightened, but still try to end it. For her country, and for the greater good.

slayer.description: The Entrenched knows the uniform before she knows anything else about the man wearing it: Ostvengr's Slayer corps, the most disciplined and deadly force on any battlefield. That this one was sealed in a box before she was born does not signify. He is a national enemy, and it is her duty to see him bombarded to death.

succubus.description: The Exorcist will feel the Succubus working on him and will know precisely what she is, a demon who must be exorcised. Discipline and long practice will hold the door against her charms, but only barely.

vestal.description: The Flagellant remembers the Vestal from his time in the Abbey—one who fled her divine retribution rather than embracing sacred suffering. Her strength intrigued him then, but her defiance filled him with scorn and pity.

crusader.description: The heiress maintains a reserved, professional demeanor towards the crusader, her latest recruit.

duchess.description: The Heiress remembers the Duchess as aloof and self-absorbed during the few balls they attended together before the woman disappeared from court. Years and a bloodsucker transformation later, the Heiress doesn't recognise her.

highwayman.description: The Heiress recognizes the Highwayman's value as a skilled fighter and tracker, though his criminal background requires she remain watchful. She hired him for competence, not trustworthiness.

hqclaimants.description: The Heiress vaguely recalls the Claimants from years ago—a pair of nobles who spent the Ancestor's parties ingratiating themselves to her father. They said something dismissive to her once, she thinks, but she can barely remember their faces now.

kheir.description: The Heiress maintains a sharp-tongued rapport with her brother, quick to criticize his anxieties in private but equally quick to defend him from others. Beneath the cutting remarks lies fierce protectiveness.

snake_charmer.description: The letter that dragged the Heiress from her studies and made her responsible for all of this was apparently not written to her alone. Her Ancestor sent the same appeal to some order of snake handlers in a desert she cannot place on a map, and one of them has now walked in and offered his help. Her claim to this place is supposed to be a matter of blood.

thorn.description: Swordplay as entertainment never interested the Heiress, and celebrated champions belonged to her father's social world, not hers. If she ever shared a room with the famous duelist, no memory of it survives.

thrall.description: Thanks to the machinations of her eminent Ancestor, this monster is hers—though she does not know it yet. The papers bearing her Estate's seal will arrive with him.

voivode.description: A foreign lord will arrive claiming the Ancestor as a personal friend. He will offer assistance the Heiress did not ask for and speaks fondly of the old chapel that now lies in ruins near the Dower House.

crusader.description: The Highwayman sees in the Crusader another man seeking redemption through violence. He hopes this stern warrior might understand the weight of a violent past better than most.

heiress.description: The Highwayman is determined to prove his worth to the Heiress and earn a place in her service, seeing this quest as his path to redemption.

kheir.description: The Highwayman takes his role as the Heir's guard seriously, viewing the nervous scholar's safety as part of his quest for absolution.

duchess.description: The Claimants viewed the Duchess as a social rival whose pride and influence stood in the way of their own ambitions at court.

heiress.description: The Claimants remember the Heiress as an afterthought at her father's side during courtly functions—sharp-tongued but provincial, a minor irritation easily dismissed while they pursued more valuable connections.

kheir.description: The Claimants cultivated connections with the Heir's father during the Ancestor's gatherings, finding the bloodline useful for their ambitions. The boy himself was hardly worth acknowledging—naive and eager, forever trailing in his father's (and sister's) shadow.

psychiatrist.description: The Claimants recall the Therapist as a prestigious but forgettable court employee. His true value was the curious tome they stole from his collection—the very book that guided them to the Estate. To them, the man was merely a means to a much grander end.

thorn.description: The sister found the celebrated court champion beneath notice—a commoner performer, however decorated. The brother paid closer attention, in his way: he rated her skill honestly and dismissed her discipline entirely, dueling being play-war for spectators while real wars are won with polearms and formations. Her maiming struck them both as an unremarkable end to an unserious pursuit.

wretch.description: The Claimants witnessed the Wretch's fall, finding amusement at the minor noble family's spectacular disgrace. His new life in the sewers only heightens their amusement.

crusader.description: The Heir is intimidated by the Crusader's imposing presence and martial bearing, but finds some comfort in having such a formidable protector.

duchess.description: As a young man, the Heir was captivated by the Duchess's elegance and fencing prowess at court, back when she was human. Their interactions were brief and unreciprocated, but her image lingered in his mind for years. He worried for her when she, along with the others who attended the Ancestor's final debauch, vanished from society.

greymane.description: The Heir has read what little reaches the Kingdom about a small country that closed its borders a generation ago: a siege it should not have survived, and a king who answered it with a curse that took his own people too. None of the accounts are firsthand, and he assumed the king died with the kingdom.

heiress.description: The Heir both admires and envies his sister's boldness, feeling perpetually caught between pride in her achievements and inadequacy at his own. Despite their constant bickering, he trusts her completely.

highwayman.description: The Heir is deeply uncomfortable around the rough-mannered Highwayman, finding his criminal past and casual violence unsettling despite his sister's trust in hiring him.

hqclaimants.description: The Heir met the Claimants at the Ancestor's parties—they were always hovering around his father, flattering him with talk of lineage and legacy. When they deigned to notice the Heir himself, their remarks were cutting and condescending. Sometimes he wonders if they remain as insufferable as he remembers.

leper.description: The Heir read of the Leper and the kingdom he once ruled, though the accounts of his abdication were frustratingly vague. He wonders what truly happened.

musketeer.description: The Heir is aware through family records that the Musketeer's bloodline and his own share distant ancestry, though the connection is generations removed.

thorn.description: The Heir attended the famed duelist's exhibitions during his courtly years, admiring the spectacle the way bookish young men admire any effortless mastery. He remembers the scandal of her blinding—how quickly the court's delight curdled into gossip—and that she vanished from society afterward. He assumed, like everyone, that her story had ended there.

voivode.description: The Heir keeps the Estate's old records, and the Voivode's name appears in them—a guest of the house, entertained more than once. It also appears in ledgers far older than that, in the same hand and with the same title. He has assumed a family of foreign lords sharing a name, and will have to revise that assumption.

succubus.description: The Lamia wears a borrowed face herself, and will recognise another glamour on sight. She will not be charmed by it.

thrall.description: The Lamia sat among the spectators at the pit-fighter's last match, and watched the beloved champion crushed to pulp—watched the adoring crowd turn, in a breath, into a mob. She knows better than most how quickly worship curdles, though that day she watched as one of the crowd.

duchess.description: The Maid came to the Estate and its courtyard to find her Mistress, who attended the Ancestor's final ball and never came back. The Duchess was at that ball, and while she did get infected, she survived with her wits intact. Maybe there is hope the Maid's Mistress did, too?

eagle.description: Bird-folk all look alike to the Man-at-Arms, but he remembers the Arbiter. Years into wandering with nothing but his own regret, he came upon a squad of deserters being gunned down by their own kind and pulled two of them out. It was his first step towards redemption.

sisters.description: The Meister knows of the sisters by reputation — the general and the killer, who won a warlord victory after victory in a province the emperor's court watched with some concern. He had not expected to find only one of them standing here, and would like to know which, and what became of the other.

commandant.description: The Monitor faced Chernozem's officers across the Black Earth for fifty years and thinks well of them. The commandant here, with no war behind him, is a man without a posting. That makes him useful, and the Monitor means to make the offer early.

prefect.description: The Occultist has corresponded with the Prefect for years, and holds him in a regard he extends to almost nobody. The bird worked his own way to power that the Occultist had to bargain for, which he envies without resenting. Whichever of them reached the Estate first sent for the other.

succubus.description: The Occultist has studied the infernal courts, and will see what is under the pilgrim's robe the first time he looks at her properly. The glamour will not hold against him.

jester.description: As a girl the Omen Seeker watched a travelling musician play a tune that twisted its audience to death, and the tune has haunted her ever since. That same musician later taught the tune to the Jester in a graveyard. She knows none of this, only that there is a shape in the Jester's ballad that terrifies her.

sibyl_ms.description: The Omen Seeker has burned villages and covens of non-believers like the Sibyl, and her current doubt in herself does not undo the past.

occultist.description: The Prefect and the Occultist have written to one another for years, on matters neither would discuss with a colleague of ordinary nerve. The Prefect thinks well of him: a serious mind working without a university behind him, which he considers the harder road. Whichever of them reached the Estate first sent for the other.

hqclaimants.description: The Psychiatrist holds a unique contempt for his former employers, whom he found insufferably vain. This professional disdain turned to cold fury when they stole a dangerous tome from his library, and he now sees them as reckless thieves meddling with forces they cannot comprehend.

slayer.description: The Slayer corps and the Kaisergarde went together into the Maw of Darkness. When the Rampart and others were infected, they gave everything to seal the parasites away, while the Slayer's deception threatened the entire country. The Rampart remembers him and his transgression.

thrall.description: The Ringmaster will recognise his potential as a headliner. Enormous, obedient, and capable of a frenzy no crowd would ever forget. She will want him in the Butcher's Circus.

crusader.description: The Seraph valued the Crusader as a capable commander whose devotion to the Light seemed unquestioned. His mercy toward the Warlord and subsequent departure from the crusade marked him as another soul too weak to uphold righteous judgment.

sibyl_ms.description: The Light orders the Seraph to cleanse all heretics, and this 'Sibyl' will be no exception.

crusader.description: The Sibyl worships the Radiance, another beaten branch of the same faith, and a former rival of the Light. Crusades the Crusader marched with were sent to snuff them out for good. Walking in search of other survivors, her hatred for their annihilators will never fade.

omenseeker.description: The Inquisition of the Flame burns all who do not follow the Light, the Sibyl's people among them. The Sibyl hates them for what they do.

seraph.description: The Sibyl worships the Radiance, another beaten branch of the same faith, and a former rival of the Light. Crusades led by the Seraph were sent to snuff them out for good. Walking in search of other survivors, her hatred for their annihilators will never fade.

meister.description: The Sisters heard of the boy in the emperor's court, appointed absurdly young, and assumed he had died with the rest of it. Finding him alive and this far west is a surprise; finding him certain that nothing under the Estate is worth having is a disappointment.

rampart.description: The Ostvengr Kaisergarde and the Slayer corps went down into the Maw together, and most of the survivors came back carrying eldritch parasites. Though the Slayer tried to fight it, the empire sealed them both away, one in a shell and the other in a casket.

heiress.description: The Snake Charmer's Master gave a lifetime to studying the thing beneath this house, and was written to as an equal. The same summons went to a young woman who inherited the address along with the furniture and has no training at all. That the summons made her the authority here strikes him as an error.

psychiatrist.description: The Succubus will recognise him at once: this man serves Paimon, a demonic king of the infernal court. She will offer him insights, and he who usually manipulates others will not realise he is the one being played.

seraph.description: One of the Succubus' congregations came apart exactly as it was meant to: rumour, then suspicion, then schism, and a witch hunter named Mathis kept on a short leash. Burning the girl at the centre of it was supposed to end the work. It did not.

voivode.description: The Succubus has known him for centuries and has never once been impressed. He was a provincial lord who bought immortality and has spent it since telling everyone about it. She likes him anyway, in the way one likes an old dog, and she will accept his protection without thanking him for it.

resonant.description: When she was a god, the Tempest sometimes felt what the Resonant now claims to see, and dismissed it. She will dismiss it again. If the world is a design, then her pantheon were pieces in it too, and her fall was nobody's betrayal.

duchess.description: The Thorn once knew the court's finest fencer—her great rival, their match forever anticipated and never fought. Beneath curse-wrought armor, a changed voice, and a monstrous blade no fencer would carry, there would be nothing left for a blind woman to recognize. Though perhaps something in the cadence of the footwork might nag at her, like a name on the tip of the tongue.

hqclaimants.description: A hundred noble voices flattered or sneered from beyond the piste, long since run together. One she does remember: a military man who lectured her, uninvited, that fencing was a game and real wars were won with pikes. She recalls composing several retorts she was never permitted to deliver.

heiress.description: The Thrall knows the name of the house that owns him now, and came to serve it. Another master among the many; no closer to freedom than the day he was branded.

ringmaster.description: The Thrall has seen many like the Ringmaster. On her cues, he is to maim someone beyond recognition. Applause will follow.

flagellant.description: The Vestal remembers the tortures the Flagellant inflicted in the Abbey's dungeons, the punisher for her failures. To her, he represented the cruelty of blind devotion—a symbol of what she overcame and now stands against.

seraph.description: Even within the Abbey's walls, the Vestal heard whispered legends of the Seraph—a warrior-saint burned at the stake who rose transformed by divine fire. Her divine purpose shows the Light's true path.

heiress.description: The Voivode came here for the Ancestor, and his descendants are of small concern. He will indulge them out of respect for his old friend, and appraise them for his flock while he is at it. He will find a part of his friend's arrogance in the Heiress.

kheir.description: The Voivode came here for the Ancestor, and his descendants are of small concern. He will indulge them out of respect for his old friend, and appraise them for his flock while he is at it. He will find a part of his friend's diligence in the Heir.

psychiatrist.description: The Voivode will place the Therapist quickly: a mortal in a bargain, doing careful work for a lord of the infernal court. He respects the craft and will attempt to invite him to dinner and eventually to the goblet. A man who understands contracts is a far better prospect than the frightened peasants he usually recruits.

succubus.description: The Voivode has known the Succubus for centuries and remembers her fondly, from a time when they hunted the same courts and dined on the same souls. He serves a king and she a duke, which by his reckoning settles the matter of rank between them. He looks forward to good company and to being treated, for once, as what he is.

zenith.description: Sol Invictus is a dying faith, and the Sunlight Warrior long ago accepted that he would outlive it and go on as its last devotee. But this Zenith, wearing its sun and holding to its four virtues, proves him otherwise. For now, at least.

hqclaimants.description: The Wretch remembers the Claimants from his days at court—ambitious nobles who embodied everything he once aspired to be. Though the bitterness has long since faded among his rats, their presence is an uncomfortable reminder of the life he abandoned.

warrior_of_sunlight.description: The Zenith grew up on a story his order told itself: that somewhere out there a knight still walks the Kingdom praising a sun that was driven out of it generations ago, and has never stopped. It was a comfort, not a claim. He had not expected to meet the man.
